h1: Bette bathroom installation in Stoke Poges

hero.intro: Large plots and substantial houses define much of Stoke Poges, from the period detached homes near Stoke Park to the executive-style builds further out on sizeable gardens set well back from the road. That extra room to manoeuvre matters when the bath being installed is a Bette: a titanium-steel shell finished in fused glass enamel, harder and more scratch-resistant than acrylic, but entirely dependent on the substructure underneath it being built properly. We install Bette baths and shower trays with the levelling, bracing and acoustic isolation that material actually calls for, and the generous footprint typical of Stoke Poges properties usually gives us more scope to reposition a waste run or widen a doorway than a terraced house would allow.

sections.heading: The Bette material, and what it demands of an installation
sections.body: Bette manufactures baths and shower trays from titanium-steel finished with fused glass enamel, a combination that's harder and more scratch-resistant than the acrylic used in most retail bathroom ranges. That durability comes with a trade-off: the material is unforgiving of a poorly built base underneath it. A titanium-steel shell doesn't flex to absorb an uneven floor or a slightly out-of-level stud wall the way acrylic can; any movement in the substructure shows up as noise, a hairline stress point, or a shell that never quite sits flat against its surround. We treat a Bette bath or shower tray as a different job from a standard acrylic fitting from the first-fix stage onward, not as a drop-in swap.

sections.heading: Where Stoke Poges properties give us more room to work
sections.body: Stoke Poges is a village of large plots and substantial houses, and Stoke Park's golf and country club gives the area its best-known identity. The housing around it ranges from older period detached homes to more recent executive-style builds, many set well back from the road on sizeable gardens. That scale generally gives us far more room to manoeuvre on layout than a smaller property would allow. Relocating a waste run to suit a Bette bath's outlet position, widening a doorway for level access, or adding a second en-suite off a principal bedroom rarely runs into the structural constraints a terraced house would present, which keeps the installation programme more predictable from the outset.

sections.heading: Levelling, bracing and acoustic isolation: what actually happens under a Bette
sections.body: Fitting a Bette properly starts below the shell, not with the shell itself. We build and level a dedicated substructure sized to the bath or tray's exact footprint, brace the frame so the steel can't flex or rock once it's loaded with water and a bather's weight, and isolate it acoustically so the enamel surface doesn't transmit every knock and footstep through the floor below. Skipping any one of those steps is how a Bette ends up with a hollow sound, a loose feel underfoot, or movement at the waste connection within a few months. We don't treat it like any other bath, because the manufacturer doesn't design it to be treated like any other bath.

sections.heading: How a fit-only Bette install runs, start to finish
sections.body: We work fit-only: you choose and buy the Bette bath or shower tray, along with your brassware, tiles and furniture, and we handle everything from strip-out onward. It starts with a paid survey at £125, where we check floor structure, waste positions, access routes and the doorway widths a Stoke Poges property's layout allows, and confirm what the substructure will need to look like for your chosen model. From there we strip out the old bathroom, carry out first-fix plumbing and any structural adjustments, build and tile around the new substructure, install the bath or tray, connect brassware, and snag the finished room before we leave. Installs start from £3,500, reflecting the extra groundwork a Bette shell needs compared with a standard acrylic fitting.

sections.heading: Get a survey booked
sections.body: If you're planning a bathroom around a Bette bath or shower tray in Stoke Poges, the sensible next step is a survey, so we can see the floor, the waste run and the access route before any work is priced or scheduled. Call or WhatsApp 07399 651836 to arrange one.

faqs.q: Why does a Bette bath need a different substructure to an acrylic one?
faqs.a: Titanium-steel finished with fused glass enamel doesn't flex the way acrylic does, so any unevenness or movement in the floor beneath it shows up as noise or stress on the shell instead of being absorbed. We build a level, braced, acoustically isolated base sized to the specific bath or tray before it goes in.

faqs.q: Do I need to buy the Bette bath myself?
faqs.a: Yes. We work fit-only, so you buy the bath, shower tray, brassware, tiles and furniture, and we handle the strip-out, first-fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging.

faqs.q: Does Stoke Poges' larger plot sizes actually change the installation?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The space around typical Stoke Poges properties gives us more flexibility to move a waste run, widen a doorway for level access, or add a second en-suite off a principal bedroom than a terraced house layout would allow.

faqs.q: How much does a Bette installation cost?
faqs.a: Installs start from £3,500. The exact price depends on the scope of work, including the substructure a Bette bath or tray needs, and is confirmed after the £125 survey.

We check the floor structure, waste positions, access routes and doorway widths, and confirm what substructure, levelling and acoustic isolation your chosen Bette model will need before any work is scheduled.

faqs.q: Do you install Bette shower trays as well as baths?
faqs.a: Yes, both. Bette manufactures shower trays in the same titanium-steel and fused glass enamel finish as its baths, and they need the same attention to levelling and substructure underneath.
